notes: A three-floor escape tower where each sealed floor holds you until its challenge is solved is the Escape Room preset, but no catalogue shape describes it: rooms-sequence is chambers joined by corridors on one level while these three sit directly above each other, interior-single is one enclosed space, course-tower does stack but is a jump course rather than puzzle rooms, and world-underground is the same stacking read downward from a surface map. So it is a described shape, interior-only and stacked, which is what puts P2 on the route; the tower is one contiguous structure rather than separate maps, so zone-count stays single and no P4 is added. Adventure is named second because it supplies the damage source as hazard-kill and, more importantly, checkpoint-respawn for the one-shot revive item that returns a player to the floor they died on instead of floor 1, while gate-progression is the elevator or stairs each solve unlocks and gate-solve is the roof exit that ends the run. Decided without a user: the per-floor puzzle mechanics and the three distinct cartoon-adventure themes are mine to choose as the author delegated them, the never-sent second message is ignored on the author's instruction, and the Luau script, HUD and per-player progress isolation are mechanics that leave the layout unchanged.
